chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text: This policy establishes a consistent method for earning, requesting, approving, using, carrying over, and recording paid time off (PTO). PTO is intended for planned vacation, personal appointments, rest, and other discretionary time away from work. Medical, statutory, caregiving, bereavement, and other protected absences are handled under **POL-LEV-001** and must not be incorrectly classified as vacation.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text: This policy applies to employees whose offer letter or employment agreement identifies them as Regular Full-Time (RFT) or Regular Part-Time (RPT). Temporary employees, interns, agency workers, and contractors receive PTO only when a written agreement or applicable law says so. Where law or a signed agreement provides a greater right, the greater right applies.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
- **Business day:** Monday through Friday, excluding a holiday on the employee's assigned holiday calendar.
- **Scheduled workday:** A day the employee is expected to work under the approved schedule.
- **PTO day:** Eight hours for administrative conversion. Actual deductions use the employee's scheduled hours for the day.
- **Service year:** Completed continuous service measured from the employee's recognized service date.
- **Available balance:** Accrued PTO shown in the HR system, less approved future requests and any adjustments.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
PTO accrues each pay period from the employee's recognized service date. New hires receive a prorated accrual for the remainder of the calendar year. Employees may use accrued PTO after 30 calendar days of employment unless People Operations approves an earlier use or applicable law requires otherwise.
| Employment category and completed service | Annual full-time entitlement | Administrative hours |
|---|---:|---:|
| RFT, less than 5 completed years | 15 days | 120 hours |
| RFT, 5 through 9 completed years | 20 days | 160 hours |
| RFT, 10 or more completed years | 25 days | 200 hours |
| RPT, 20-29 scheduled hours per week | Prorated from the applicable service tier | Tier hours x scheduled weekly hours / 40 |
Service-tier increases take effect at the start of the pay period containing the employee's service anniversary. Accrual continues during paid leave. Accrual may pause after 30 consecutive calendar days of unpaid leave unless law, a benefit plan, or a written leave approval requires continuation.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
1. PTO may be used only against scheduled work time.
2. Company holidays are not deducted from PTO.
3. PTO may be requested in half-day increments. A smaller increment may be used when required by law, an approved accommodation, or a local timekeeping rule.
4. Employees may not create a negative PTO balance. People Operations may approve an advance of up to 16 hours only for a documented payroll correction or exceptional business transition; this is not a routine benefit.
5. Employees must not perform work while recorded as on PTO unless a manager asks the employee to address an urgent matter and the PTO record is corrected.
6. PTO does not replace required attendance, performance, or availability expectations.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
Requests must be submitted through the approved HR system and include dates, partial-day details, and any known coverage plan.
| Consecutive PTO requested | Normal minimum notice |
|---|---:|
| 1-2 scheduled workdays | 5 business days |
| 3-5 scheduled workdays | 10 business days |
| 6 or more scheduled workdays | 20 business days |
Unexpected needs should be reported to the manager as soon as reasonably possible. Short notice does not automatically disqualify a request, but approval may depend on coverage and business impact.
The employee's manager is the normal approver. A manager requesting more than 10 consecutive business days requires approval from the next-level manager and People Operations. People Operations may review any request involving a policy exception, overlapping leave, or an inaccurate balance.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
Managers must consider operational coverage, customer commitments, deadlines, fairness across the team, prior approvals, and the employee's opportunity to use accrued time. Approval must not be withheld for a discriminatory or retaliatory reason.
When requests conflict, managers should first seek voluntary alternatives. If no alternative is available, the manager may consider the order of complete requests, critical role coverage, prior high-demand approvals, and equitable rotation. A "first come, first served" rule is not absolute.
Teams may establish limited critical-period restrictions only with director and People Operations approval and at least 30 calendar days' notice. Restrictions must identify the business reason, dates, affected roles, and an exception path.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.section_title: Changes, cancellation, and illness during PTO
chunk.text:
Employees must promptly update a request when dates change. Managers should avoid canceling approved PTO. If a documented business emergency requires cancellation, the director and People Operations must approve the change, and reasonable non-refundable costs caused solely by the cancellation may be reviewed under **POL-EXP-001**.
An employee who becomes ill or experiences another qualifying event during approved PTO may ask People Operations to reclassify eligible days under **POL-LEV-001**. Supporting information may be required, but the employee should not disclose more medical information than necessary.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
Up to 40 hours of unused PTO may carry into the next calendar year. Carried hours should be used by March 31. Unused carryover after March 31 expires unless law, a written agreement, or a documented inability to take approved PTO requires a different result.
Managers must review high balances by October 1 and create a reasonable use plan with the employee. Employees remain responsible for submitting requests; a high balance does not create automatic approval for specific dates.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text: Unused PTO is paid, forfeited, or otherwise treated according to applicable law and the employee's written agreement. The HR system calculation must be reviewed when an employee changes between full-time and part-time status, transfers jurisdictions, or has a corrected service date.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
- **Employee:** Maintain accurate requests, provide reasonable notice, monitor the balance, and coordinate coverage.
- **Manager:** Decide requests consistently, document exceptions, protect employees from retaliation, and support reasonable use of accrued PTO.
- **People Operations:** Maintain rules and balances, resolve disputes, interpret interactions with leave and law, and audit adjustments.
- **Payroll:** Process approved balances and separation payments using authorized records.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States; greater legal or signed-agreement rights prevail.
chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text: Policy exceptions require People Operations approval and, when they materially affect cost or coverage, director approval. Questions or disputes may be submitted under **POL-HRC-001**. PTO requests, approvals, adjustments, and balance transactions are retained in the HR system according to the corporate records schedule.

chunk.policy_title: Paid Time Off and Vacation Policy
chunk.text:
- An employee requesting three scheduled workdays next week should normally provide 10 business days' notice, confirm sufficient available balance, and obtain manager approval.
- A holiday occurring during a five-day vacation is not deducted from PTO.
- An employee with 24 available hours cannot submit a 32-hour request unless the dates are changed or a rare advance is approved.
- A six-week absence is not automatically a PTO matter. People Operations must determine whether part of the time is leave, an approved extended vacation, or another arrangement.

chunk.text: This policy defines company holiday calendars, floating holidays, substitute days, work performed on a holiday, and closures caused by weather, building conditions, public emergencies, or company decisions.

chunk.applicability: Employees assigned to a Northstar Canada or United States holiday calendar.
chunk.text:
Each employee is assigned a holiday calendar based on the Registered Home Office in the HR system, not the employee's temporary travel location. Vancouver and Toronto employees normally follow the Canada calendar. Seattle and Austin employees normally follow the United States calendar. A written employment agreement or local legal requirement may create a different calendar.
People Operations publishes the next year's calendar by December 1. A calendar may be updated when a government changes an observed date or when Northstar designates an additional closure.

chunk.applicability: Employees assigned to a Northstar Canada or United States holiday calendar.
chunk.text:
RFT employees receive holiday pay for the scheduled hours that would normally be worked, up to eight hours, unless a local rule provides more. RPT employees receive holiday pay when the holiday falls on a normally scheduled workday, prorated to the scheduled hours, unless law requires another calculation.
Temporary employees and interns receive holiday pay only when required by law or stated in a written agreement. Contractors are not employees and do not receive company holiday pay.

chunk.text:
When a fixed-date holiday falls on a weekend, the published calendar identifies the observed weekday. Employees must use the published date rather than independently selecting another day.
An employee required and preapproved to work on a company holiday may receive a substitute paid day, premium pay, or another legally required treatment. The manager must consult People Operations before promising a specific result. A substitute day should normally be used within 60 calendar days.

chunk.applicability: Employees assigned to a Northstar Canada or United States holiday calendar.
chunk.text: A paid company holiday during approved PTO is recorded as a holiday and is not deducted from the employee's PTO balance. Holiday pay during a statutory, medical, personal, or unpaid leave is determined under **POL-LEV-001**, the relevant benefit plan, and applicable law.

chunk.applicability: Employees assigned to a Northstar Canada or United States holiday calendar.
chunk.text:
Northstar may close a physical office or announce a delayed opening because of severe weather, utility failure, unsafe building conditions, transportation disruption, public emergency, or another material risk.
- Employees able to work safely from an approved location should normally work remotely unless the closure notice states that operations are suspended.
- Employees who cannot work remotely must contact their manager. People Operations will determine pay or time-recording treatment based on employment status, local requirements, and the closure notice.
- Employees must not travel to a closed office to retrieve equipment without Facilities or Security approval.
- A school or dependent-care closure does not automatically close Northstar. Employees should discuss PTO, flexible hours, or leave options with the manager.

chunk.applicability: Employees assigned to a Northstar Canada or United States holiday calendar.
chunk.text: Some support, security, infrastructure, and customer operations may require holiday coverage. Managers must identify essential coverage in advance, use an equitable rotation where practical, and confirm time-recording or substitute-day treatment before the shift.

chunk.applicability: Employees assigned to a Northstar Canada or United States holiday calendar.
chunk.text: An employee who needs time away for an observance not on the assigned calendar may use the floating holiday, PTO, a schedule adjustment, unpaid time, or an accommodation. Requests are handled individually and must not be denied for a discriminatory or retaliatory reason.

chunk.text: People Operations owns the calendars. Managers communicate coverage and approve floating holidays. Employees verify their assigned calendar and promptly report an incorrect assignment. Holiday calendars, closure notices, substitute-day approvals, and pay adjustments are retained in the HR or payroll system.

- A Toronto employee on PTO from December 24 through December 31, 2026 is not charged PTO for December 25 or December 28.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: This policy establishes work-location designations, eligibility, approval, schedule, performance, safety, security, equipment, and travel expectations for remote and hybrid work. It does not authorize work outside the employee's registered province, state, or country; those requests are governed by **POL-INT-001**.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Every employee record must contain one of the following designations and a Registered Home Office.
| Designation | Normal expectation |
|---|---|
| Office-Based | Works primarily from the assigned office. Occasional remote work of up to two days per calendar month may be approved by the manager. |
| Hybrid | Works from the assigned office at least two days per week or the greater team standard, and from the approved home workspace on other approved days. |
| Remote | Works primarily from the approved home workspace and attends planned onsite events or customer locations when required. |
A manager may set common team anchor days. A designation is not an entitlement and does not prevent reasonable changes for business, performance, security, accommodation, or legal reasons.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
A new or changed designation requires a documented request, manager recommendation, and People Operations approval. Information Security approval is also required when the role regularly handles Restricted data outside an office.
Approved arrangements are reviewed at least annually and when the employee changes role, manager, home address, jurisdiction, performance status, or client assignment. Silence or informal past practice is not approval.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Remote work may occur only at the approved home workspace or another location expressly approved for the relevant dates. The employee must keep the residential address and Registered Home Office current in the HR system.
Any work outside the registered province or state, including within the same country, must be assessed under **POL-INT-001** before travel. Working from another country while on personal vacation is still work and requires approval.
Public cafes, hotel lobbies, shared lounges, and transportation terminals are not approved locations for handling Confidential or Restricted information. A private coworking space may be approved when Security and the manager confirm appropriate controls.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Employees must follow an approved schedule and comply with timekeeping requirements. Unless a team has a different documented schedule, employees must be available during core collaboration hours of 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. in the employee's Registered Home Office time zone.
Remote work is not a substitute for dependent care during working hours. Brief, incidental interruptions are expected in normal life; recurring care needs require an approved schedule, PTO, or leave arrangement.
Employees must maintain calendar visibility, attend required meetings, respond within reasonable team norms, and notify the manager of outages or material schedule changes.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Performance, attendance, conduct, confidentiality, and customer-service standards are the same regardless of location. Managers should assess results and behavior rather than online presence alone. Surveillance tools may not be installed or used outside approved security and compliance processes.
A remote arrangement may be modified or ended when documented performance, collaboration, security, customer, or operational needs cannot be resolved. When practical, Northstar provides reasonable notice and an opportunity to discuss alternatives. Immediate changes may be required for a security, safety, legal, or client risk.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
The employee must maintain a reasonably safe, private, and functional workspace with adequate lighting, seating, electrical capacity, and internet access. Work-related injuries must be reported promptly to the manager and People Operations, even when they occur at home.
Northstar may request a self-assessment, photographs of company equipment placement, or a virtual ergonomic review. Northstar will not routinely inspect a residence without consent, but may require a different approved location when material risks cannot be addressed.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Employees must comply with **POL-SEC-001**, including company-managed device, multifactor authentication, VPN, screen privacy, storage, printing, and incident-reporting rules. Household members and visitors must not use company devices or view non-public company information.
Confidential conversations require a private setting and a headset when others may overhear. Paper containing Confidential or Restricted information should not be printed at home unless expressly approved and securely destroyed.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: Company equipment, home-office accessories, furniture reimbursement, internet stipends, repair, loss, and return are governed by **POL-EQP-001**. Reimbursements require compliance with **POL-EXP-001**. Employees should not purchase equipment with an expectation of reimbursement before receiving required approval.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.section_title: Travel to an office or customer site
chunk.text:
Normal travel between a Hybrid or Office-Based employee's residence and assigned office is commuting and is not reimbursable. Required travel by a Remote-designated employee to an office more than 50 kilometres or 30 miles from the approved home workspace is business travel when preapproved.
Remote employees may be required to attend up to four planned onsite events per calendar year with reasonable notice. Additional travel may be required by the role or employment agreement.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: Employees should maintain a practical continuity plan for short internet or power outages. This may include a company-approved hotspot, alternate approved workspace, adjusted hours, PTO, or office attendance. Employees must not use an insecure location solely to remain online.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
- **Employee:** Maintain accurate location information, protect data, meet schedule and performance expectations, and report incidents.
- **Manager:** Assess role suitability consistently, define team norms, monitor outcomes, and escalate jurisdiction or security questions.
- **People Operations:** Approve designations, maintain records, coordinate accommodations, and interpret policy.
- **Information Security and IT:** Define technical controls, approve exceptions, and support secure equipment and access.

chunk.applicability: Employees with an office, hybrid, or remote work designation in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
- A Hybrid employee may not independently work from another province for three weeks. The request must be reviewed under **POL-INT-001**.
- A Remote employee using a private home office may handle Confidential information on a company-managed device with required security controls.
- An Office-Based employee may request an occasional remote day, but repeated weekly remote work requires a designation review.
- A Remote employee required to attend a company summit in another city may claim preapproved business travel; a Hybrid employee's normal trip to the assigned office is commuting.

chunk.text:
This policy manages legal, tax, payroll, immigration, information-security, insurance, client, and operational risks when an employee proposes to work outside the province, state, or country recorded as the employee's Registered Home Office.
Approval is case-specific, revocable, and not guaranteed. Approval does not change the employee's employment location, payroll jurisdiction, compensation, benefits, or right to work unless a separate written agreement says so.

chunk.applicability: Employees performing work outside their registered province or state, domestically or internationally.
chunk.text: The policy applies whenever an employee performs any work outside the registered province or state, including email, meetings, coding, customer support, or document access during personal travel. It applies to domestic and international locations. Pure vacation with no work is not covered, but **POL-PTO-001** still applies.

chunk.applicability: Employees performing work outside their registered province or state, domestically or internationally.
chunk.text:
- **Domestic out-of-jurisdiction work:** Work in another province or state within the employee's payroll country.
- **International work:** Work in a country other than the employee's payroll country.
- **Business day worked:** Any day on which the employee performs more than incidental work, regardless of hours.
- **Standard-Risk location:** A location currently permitted for routine review under the country-risk framework.
- **Enhanced-Review location:** A location requiring additional Legal, Security, insurance, client, or export-control assessment.
- **Prohibited location:** A location from which Northstar does not permit work because required controls or legal conditions cannot be met.

Employees performing work outside their registered province or state, domestically or internationally.
chunk.section_title: Duration categories, notice, and normal limits
chunk.text:
| Category | Duration | Normal advance notice | Normal decision path |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Domestic short-term | 1-10 business days in a rolling 90 days | 10 business days | Manager + People Operations acknowledgment |
| Domestic extended | 11-30 business days in a rolling 12 months | 20 business days | Manager + director + People Operations + Payroll/Tax + Security |
| International short-term | 1-20 business days in a rolling 12 months | 20 business days | Manager + director + People Operations + Security + Finance/Tax |
| International exceptional | 21-30 business days in a rolling 12 months | 30 business days | All short-term approvals + VP sponsor + Legal review |
| Assignment or location change | More than 30 business days, recurring residence, or permanent move | At least 60 calendar days | Formal mobility, transfer, or employment-location process; not a temporary-work approval |
The normal aggregate limit is 30 domestic out-of-jurisdiction business days and 20 international business days in any rolling 12-month period. An international period of 21-30 days is exceptional and requires a documented business or compelling personal rationale. Days need not be consecutive to count.

Personal-travel costs are not reimbursable. Business costs require preapproval under **POL-EXP-001**. The employee is responsible for personal travel documents and personal tax advice unless the request is a company-directed assignment.
An employee who cannot return as planned must contact the manager and People Operations before continuing work. An emergency extension is not automatic; work may be suspended until required approvals are obtained.

chunk.text: A British Columbia employee asking to work from Germany for six calendar weeks would normally propose about 30 business days. Employees submit complete, accurate requests and follow all conditions. Managers assess business feasibility and coverage. People Operations coordinates the review and retains the decision. Security, Finance/Tax, Legal, and client owners assess risks within their authority. chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text: This policy establishes minimum information-security controls for remote, hybrid, mobile, and international work. It protects Northstar, employee, customer, and partner information while enabling approved work outside a controlled office.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
| Classification | Examples | Remote-work rule |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Published website, approved press release, public job posting | May be handled in ordinary approved business tools |
| Internal | Internal procedures, routine team notes, non-sensitive project plans | Use approved accounts and services; avoid unnecessary local copies |
| Confidential | Employee records, customer information, contracts, source code, non-public financial data | Company-managed device, MFA, encryption, and approved storage required |
| Restricted | Authentication secrets, highly sensitive HR investigations, regulated data, production keys, security incident evidence | Explicit access authorization and enhanced controls; no remote printing or unapproved international access |
When uncertain, employees must treat information as Confidential until the owner or Security confirms otherwise.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
The company VPN must be used when required by the application, Security notice, or data classification. Home Wi-Fi must use WPA2 or stronger security with a non-default administrator password.
Public Wi-Fi should be avoided. When no safer option exists, the employee must use a company hotspot or VPN and must not access Restricted information. Captive portals, shared hotel business centres, public computers, and unknown charging/data cables must not be used for company work.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
Employees must position screens and conversations to prevent unauthorized viewing or listening. A headset and private room are required for Confidential discussions when others may overhear. Household members, guests, and service providers must not use company equipment or access company information.
Employees working in temporary lodging must secure devices when leaving the room and avoid leaving badges, notes, or equipment visible. Devices should remain in carry-on possession during travel.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
Company information must be stored in approved company repositories. Employees must not forward company information to personal email, consumer file-sharing services, personal messaging accounts, or removable media.
Printing Confidential information at home requires a documented business need and manager approval. Printing Restricted information outside a controlled office is prohibited unless Security approves a specific exception. Approved paper records must be locked when not in use and destroyed through an approved secure method.
External sharing must use approved channels, least-privilege access, an appropriate expiration date, and verification of the recipient.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
Meetings may be recorded only when participants are notified and the recording is stored in an approved location. Employees must not paste Confidential or Restricted information into public generative-AI tools, public code assistants, public translation tools, or unapproved browser extensions.
Approved enterprise AI services may be used only within their documented data-classification limits. Restricted information requires explicit Security and data-owner approval even when the tool is company licensed.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
**POL-INT-001** approval is required before working outside the registered province or state. Standard-Risk location status does not remove security requirements.
Security may require a travel device, application restrictions, read-only access, download blocking, temporary credentials, device inspection after return, or complete suspension of access. Restricted information may not be accessed outside the payroll country without explicit written Security approval.
Employees must immediately report unexpected border inspection of a company device, forced credential disclosure, device detention, or any request to install software.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
Company equipment must be protected against theft, damage, and unauthorized access. A lost or stolen device, badge, security key, or phone used for MFA must be reported to Security and the manager within one hour of discovery. Employees should not delay reporting while searching for the item.
Security may remotely lock or wipe equipment. Employees must cooperate with replacement, credential reset, incident review, and police or insurer documentation where appropriate.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
Report immediately, and no later than one hour after discovery, any suspected phishing success, malware, credential compromise, unauthorized access, accidental external sharing, misdirected email containing Confidential information, or loss of sensitive paper.
Employees should preserve evidence, stop further sharing, disconnect a device from networks when instructed, and avoid independently deleting logs or negotiating with an attacker. Security owns technical containment. People Operations owns employee-related case coordination when the incident involves HR information or conduct.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text: Northstar may log access, device health, network connections, file sharing, and security events for legitimate security, legal, and operational purposes. Monitoring must be proportionate, authorized, and consistent with applicable law. Managers may not deploy informal surveillance or require employees to keep a camera continuously active.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text: A security exception must identify the business need, data, duration, compensating controls, owner, and expiration date. The Chief Information Security Officer or delegate must approve exceptions involving Confidential or Restricted information. Convenience alone is not sufficient.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
Employees and contractors are responsible for following controls and reporting concerns promptly. Managers must not pressure staff to bypass security for speed. IT maintains devices and identity services. Security defines controls, investigates incidents, and may suspend access when needed to protect Northstar.
Violations may result in access restriction, corrective action, contract consequences, or legal referral, depending on severity and intent. Good-faith incident reporting is encouraged and will not itself be treated as misconduct.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers accessing Northstar systems or information away from an approved office.
chunk.text:
- A Remote employee may review a Confidential customer contract at home on a company laptop using approved storage and required VPN.
- An employee may not upload source code to a public AI assistant, even to debug an urgent problem.
- A traveller in Germany needs the approved international-work decision and must not access Restricted HR case files unless Security explicitly authorizes it.
- A lost phone used for MFA must be reported within one hour, even if the phone has a passcode.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: This policy defines when Northstar pays or reimburses business expenses, which approvals and evidence are required, and which costs are not reimbursable. Expenses must be reasonable, necessary, properly authorized, accurately documented, and connected to a legitimate Northstar business purpose.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
1. Use an approved supplier, booking channel, corporate card, or company-provided item when available.
2. Obtain preapproval when the category or amount requires it.
3. Choose the lowest reasonable total-cost option, considering safety, time, accessibility, and business needs.
4. Separate personal and business costs.
5. Submit accurate claims within 30 calendar days after the expense or trip.
6. Never divide a purchase to avoid an approval threshold.
Northstar may decline a cost that is excessive, personal, unsupported, late without explanation, or purchased contrary to policy.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Thresholds use the employee's normal expense currency. The CAD and USD amounts are policy equivalents, not exchange-rate conversions.
| Total commitment | Required preapproval |
|---|---|
| Below CAD 500 or USD 375 | Manager, when the category requires preapproval; otherwise normal budget authority |
| CAD 500-2,499.99 or USD 375-1,874.99 | Manager and director or designated budget owner |
| CAD 2,500 or USD 1,875 and above | Manager, VP, and Finance |
All international travel, conferences, home-office furniture, non-standard technology, gifts above the routine limit, and exceptions require preapproval regardless of amount. Approval of a budget does not automatically approve an individual expense.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
An itemized receipt is required for each expense of CAD 25/USD 20 or more and whenever Finance requests it. A card slip showing only a total is not itemized. If a receipt cannot reasonably be obtained, the employee must submit a missing-receipt declaration stating vendor, date, amount, purpose, and why the receipt is unavailable. Repeated missing receipts may be declined.
Claims must include the business purpose, attendees for hosted meals, project or cost centre, currency, taxes where shown, and proof of required preapproval. Managers should review claims within five business days.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Business travel must be booked through the approved channel when available.
- Economy airfare is standard for trips with scheduled flight time under six hours.
- Premium economy may be approved for a segment of six hours or more.
- Business class requires executive approval or an approved accommodation.
- Rail may be selected when total cost and travel time are reasonable.
- Ride-share, taxi, public transit, mileage, parking, and tolls are reimbursable when business-related and documented.
- Traffic, parking, and other personal fines are never reimbursable.
- A personal vehicle may be used only when licensed, insured, and suitable. Mileage is reimbursed at the current company rate; fuel is not separately reimbursed for the same trip.
Daily commuting between a residence and assigned office is not a business expense. Travel treatment for Remote-designated employees is described in **POL-RWK-001**.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Employees should select a safe, business-appropriate hotel within the rate displayed by the approved booking tool or obtain preapproval for a higher rate.
For overnight business travel, the guideline for employee meals is up to CAD 90 or USD 75 per day, excluding reasonable tax and tip. This is a maximum, not a per diem entitlement. Alcohol is reimbursable only for a preapproved client or company event and must be reasonable.
Hosted meals must identify attendees and business purpose. An employee may not approve the employee's own hosted-meal expense; the next-level manager must review it.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Company-standard technology is procured under **POL-EQP-001** and should not be purchased personally. Eligible Hybrid and Remote employees may request preapproval for ergonomic furniture reimbursement up to **CAD 500 or USD 375 once every 36 months**. The limit applies to the combined approved chair, desk, or ergonomic accessories in the period.
An amount above the cap is personal unless an approved workplace accommodation authorizes a different amount. A CAD 900 chair is therefore not fully reimbursable under the ordinary program: when eligibility and preapproval are confirmed, reimbursement is limited to CAD 500, with the employee responsible for the remainder.
Remote-designated employees may receive the standard monthly internet stipend defined in **POL-EQP-001**. The employee may not claim the same connectivity cost again through an expense report.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Software, devices, cloud services, and subscriptions require IT or Security review when they connect to company systems, store company information, or create recurring commitments. Personal purchases made without required review may be declined even when used for work.
Professional memberships, certifications, courses, and conferences require manager and budget approval. A reimbursement agreement may apply when the cost is material and the program is optional.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
A business gift must be lawful, infrequent, transparent, and not intended to influence a decision. Gifts to one external recipient with a total value above CAD 100 or USD 75 in a calendar year require Finance or Compliance approval. Cash and cash equivalents are prohibited.
Employees must comply with conflict-of-interest and conduct requirements in **POL-CON-001**. Government officials and regulated customers may have stricter limits; obtain Legal or Compliance review before providing anything of value.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
Claims must state the original currency and amount. The expense system applies its standard conversion method. Employees should not manually add a foreign-exchange buffer. Finance may adjust tax treatment or require additional documentation.
Approved reimbursements are normally paid through payroll or accounts payable. Processing time may depend on a complete claim, manager approval, and local payment cycles.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
An exception must be approved before purchase whenever practical and must state the business reason. Finance may audit claims, request clarification, recover overpayments, suspend card privileges, or escalate suspected fraud under **POL-HRC-001** and **POL-CON-001**.
A good-faith error should be corrected promptly. Intentional falsification, duplicate claiming, or approval circumvention may result in corrective action.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: Employees make compliant choices and submit evidence. Managers verify business purpose, reasonableness, and budget. Budget owners confirm funding. Finance sets controls, processes payments, and audits claims. IT, Security, People Operations, Legal, and Compliance review categories within their authority.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers incurring approved Northstar business expenses in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
- A CAD 900 chair for a Hybrid employee requires preapproval and is ordinarily reimbursable only up to CAD 500 once every 36 months.
- A three-day domestic trip booked through the approved tool with economy airfare, reasonable hotel, itemized receipts, and business purpose is normally eligible.
- A CAD 1,200 conference requires manager and director or budget-owner preapproval.
- A laptop purchased personally without IT approval is not reimbursable merely because it was used for work.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text: This policy explains general eligibility, enrollment timing, status changes, dependent coverage, continuation during leave, and escalation for Northstar-sponsored benefits. It does not summarize every plan term. When this policy conflicts with an insurer, retirement-plan, or other formal plan document, the formal plan document controls unless applicable law provides otherwise.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
- **Regular Full-Time (RFT):** Normally scheduled for 30 or more hours per week.
- **Regular Part-Time (RPT):** Normally scheduled for 20-29 hours per week.
- **Temporary employee or intern:** Hired for a defined period or program and not designated RFT or RPT.
- **Contractor:** A non-employee providing services under a commercial agreement.
Eligibility is based on the category in the HR system, average scheduled hours where required by the plan, location, and any written employment terms.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
| Benefit category | RFT | RPT | Temporary/intern | Contractor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Employee Assistance Program (EAP) | Eligible from start date | Eligible from start date | Eligible only if program terms include the category | Not eligible |
| Core medical, dental, and vision | Eligible, subject to waiting period and local plan | Eligible only when normally scheduled at least 25 hours/week and the local plan permits | Not eligible unless written terms say otherwise | Not eligible |
| Company-paid life and disability | Eligible where offered by local plan | Normally not eligible unless local plan or written terms say otherwise | Not eligible unless written terms say otherwise | Not eligible |
| Retirement or savings plan | Eligible when plan age/service rules are met | Eligible when plan age/service rules are met | Plan-specific | Not eligible through Northstar |
| Voluntary benefits | Plan-specific | Plan-specific | Plan-specific | Not eligible |
Applicable law may require a different result. The HR system's `benefits_status` record is the operational source for an individual employee, but plan administrators make final coverage determinations.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
For an otherwise eligible employee, core insured coverage normally begins on the first day of the calendar month after the employee completes 30 calendar days of eligible service. Example: an eligible employee starting September 10 normally has coverage effective November 1.
When a plan or local law requires earlier coverage, that requirement applies. A rehire, transfer, or status change may have special rules and must be reviewed by People Operations.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
An employee must complete required enrollment or waiver elections within 31 calendar days after the eligibility notice. Failure to act may result in default coverage, employee-only coverage, or no optional coverage, depending on the plan.
After the initial window, an employee may normally change elections only during annual open enrollment or within 31 calendar days after a qualifying life event, such as marriage, divorce, birth, adoption, or loss of other coverage. Evidence may be required.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
Eligible dependents are defined by the applicable plan. Employees are responsible for accurate dependent information and timely removal of a person who is no longer eligible. Knowingly enrolling an ineligible person may result in repayment, loss of coverage, corrective action, or insurer action.
Beneficiary designations should be reviewed after major life events. A beneficiary shown in the HR portal is not necessarily valid for every plan; employees must complete plan-specific forms when required.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
Employee premiums and contributions are deducted from payroll when the plan permits. Employees must review pay statements and report an apparent error promptly. Missed deductions may be collected prospectively or through a reasonable repayment arrangement.
Northstar may change contribution levels during open enrollment or when a plan changes, subject to notice and applicable requirements.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.section_title: Changes in hours, role, or location
chunk.text:
A change in employment category, scheduled hours, legal entity, province, state, or country may change eligibility, plan options, cost, or coverage date. The employee and manager must notify People Operations before a planned change. People Operations will provide an eligibility decision based on the applicable plan.
Temporary work approved under **POL-INT-001** does not automatically change benefits. Extended assignments or permanent moves require a separate benefits review.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
Coverage during statutory, medical, parental, personal, or other leave is determined by **POL-LEV-001**, applicable law, and plan terms. During some unpaid leaves, an employee may need to pay the employee share of premiums directly. Failure to pay after required notice may result in coverage ending where legally permitted.
Paid PTO alone does not interrupt eligibility.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text: Coverage normally ends on the date or at the end of the month specified by the applicable plan and separation notice. People Operations provides information about any conversion, continuation, or portability option for which the employee may qualify. Deadlines are controlled by the plan or law and should be acted on promptly.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
Benefits information is Confidential. Managers should not request diagnoses, claim details, or dependent medical information. People Operations and plan administrators access only information necessary to administer eligibility, enrollment, contributions, leave, or accommodation processes.
The AI assistant may report a synthetic employee's eligibility or enrollment status from mock data, but it must not invent coverage, diagnose a condition, or make a final insurer determination.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
An employee who believes a record is incorrect should submit a benefits case under **POL-HRC-001** and include the employee ID, plan, event date, expected status, and any relevant notice. People Operations will correct Northstar records when appropriate or direct the employee to the plan's formal appeal process.
An urgent loss of medication access or active treatment should be marked high priority, but a service target is not a guarantee of insurer approval.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text: Employees make timely and accurate elections, review deductions, and report changes. Managers notify People Operations of approved status changes without seeking medical details. People Operations administers eligibility and notices. Payroll processes authorized deductions. Plan administrators decide claims and plan-specific coverage.

chunk.applicability: RFT and RPT employees in Canada and the United States, subject to plan documents and applicable law.
chunk.text:
- An RFT employee who has completed the waiting period is generally eligible for core benefits, subject to enrollment and plan terms.
- An RPT employee scheduled for 22 hours per week receives the EAP and may qualify for retirement benefits, but does not ordinarily qualify for core insured benefits under this policy.
- An RPT employee scheduled for 27 hours may be eligible for core insured benefits if the local plan permits and the employee enrolls on time.
- A contractor is not eligible for employee benefits merely because the contractor works full-time hours on a project.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text: This policy provides a common process for absences that are not ordinary vacation, including statutory, medical, wellness, caregiving, parental, bereavement, civic, emergency, and personal leave. Leave rights vary by location and circumstances. Northstar will apply the greater protection required by applicable law or a written agreement.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text: Nothing in this policy limits a legally protected leave, accommodation, workers' compensation right, military or civic obligation, or other mandatory entitlement. Employees should contact People Operations because the correct classification affects pay, benefits, documentation, job protection, and records.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
RFT employees receive 80 hours of paid wellness leave each calendar year. RPT employees receive a prorated amount equal to 80 hours multiplied by scheduled weekly hours divided by 40, rounded to the nearest hour. Greater statutory paid-sick entitlement is provided when required.
Wellness leave may be used for the employee's illness, injury, medical appointment, preventive care, mental-health need, or qualifying care of a family or household member. It is separate from PTO, does not carry over, and is not paid out at separation unless law requires otherwise.
Employees should notify the manager before the scheduled start time when reasonably possible and provide an expected duration. Employees do not need to disclose a diagnosis to the manager.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
An employee who cannot work or needs intermittent time because of a medical condition should contact People Operations. People Operations will assess statutory leave, disability benefits, workplace accommodation, reduced schedule, and return-to-work requirements.
For an absence of more than three consecutive scheduled workdays, or when there is a reasonable pattern or safety need, Northstar may request appropriate documentation of functional limitations, expected duration, and ability to work. A diagnosis is requested only when necessary and lawful. Medical records are stored separately with restricted access.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.section_title: Family, caregiving, parental, and statutory leave
chunk.text:
Eligible employees may take family-responsibility, caregiving, pregnancy, parental, adoption, domestic-violence, military, public-health, or other statutory leave when the legal criteria are met. Duration, pay, notice, documentation, and benefit continuation are determined by the applicable jurisdiction and plan.
An employee should provide notice as soon as reasonably possible. People Operations will identify the available leave category and may ask only for information reasonably needed to administer it.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
Northstar provides:
- up to five paid scheduled workdays after the death of an immediate family or household member; and
- up to three paid scheduled workdays after the death of an extended family member or another person with a comparably close relationship.
"Family" is interpreted inclusively and is not limited to biological or legal relationships. Additional PTO or unpaid leave may be approved. Travel, cultural, religious, and administrative needs should be considered. Documentation is not routinely required, but People Operations may request reasonable confirmation where necessary.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.section_title: Jury, witness, election, and civic duty
chunk.text:
Northstar provides paid leave for up to 10 scheduled workdays per calendar year for required jury duty or comparable civic service, less any amount that local rules require the employee to remit. Longer service is handled according to law and may be paid or unpaid. An employee must provide the summons or notice and report any early release from service.
Voluntary political activity is not civic-duty leave and should normally use PTO or unpaid time. Employees must comply with **POL-CON-001** regarding political activity and use of company resources.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
After 12 months of service, an employee may request a personal unpaid leave of up to 30 calendar days for a compelling reason not covered by another leave. Approval is discretionary and considers duration, operational coverage, prior leaves, performance, and whether a protected leave or accommodation applies.
A personal leave longer than 30 days requires VP and People Operations approval and may require a formal employment arrangement. Employees must not use personal unpaid leave to work for a competitor or avoid a conduct process.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
When foreseeable, leave should be requested at least 30 calendar days in advance or as soon as the need is known. For an emergency, the employee or representative should notify the manager or People Operations as soon as reasonably possible.
A request should identify the expected start date, estimated duration, whether the leave may be intermittent, and a safe contact method. The employee should not send detailed medical information to a manager or a general team channel.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
People Operations will provide a written summary of whether each portion of leave is paid, unpaid, covered by wellness leave, covered by PTO at the employee's election, or supported by a benefit program.
PTO accrues during paid leave. It may pause after 30 consecutive calendar days of unpaid leave unless law or a written approval requires continuation. Benefits continue according to **POL-BEN-001**, law, and plan terms. Employees may be responsible for their normal premium share during unpaid leave.
A company holiday during leave is paid only when required by the leave classification, plan, law, or written approval.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
The employee must provide reasonable status updates and promptly report a changed return date. Managers should maintain appropriate, non-intrusive contact and must not pressure an employee to work during approved leave.
People Operations may request fitness-for-work or restriction information when lawful and job-related. Northstar will consider temporary restrictions, gradual return, schedule changes, and accommodation. An employee must not return to safety-sensitive duties contrary to a documented restriction.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text: Leave and medical information is Confidential and shared only as necessary for administration, safety, payroll, benefits, accommodation, or legal obligations. Employees will not be retaliated against for requesting or using leave in good faith, supporting another employee, or reporting a concern.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text: Northstar may investigate material inconsistencies or suspected abuse, but a manager must consult People Operations before challenging medical or protected leave. Honest errors should be corrected. Intentional falsification may lead to corrective action.

chunk.applicability: Employees in Canada and the United States, with jurisdiction-specific legal rights taking precedence.
chunk.text:
- Three days of flu should normally be recorded as wellness leave, not vacation PTO, when the employee has available wellness hours.
- A planned parental leave should be raised at least 30 days in advance when possible, but late notice caused by an early birth does not eliminate legal rights.
- A five-day bereavement period for a household member is paid under this policy and should not be deducted from PTO.
- A six-week personal absence may require a combination of protected leave, unpaid leave, PTO, or a formal arrangement; it is not automatically approved as personal leave.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: This policy establishes a consistent, secure, and welcoming onboarding process from accepted offer through the first 90 calendar days. It defines required records, access, equipment, training, role clarity, and ownership.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
- **People Operations:** Owns the onboarding case, employment records, policy notices, eligibility, and completion tracking.
- **Hiring manager:** Defines role outcomes, schedule, work designation, access needs, training, and team integration.
- **IT:** Prepares devices, accounts, standard software, and technical support.
- **Information Security:** Applies identity, access, device, and data controls and assigns security training.
- **Finance/Payroll:** Establishes payroll, tax, expense, and purchasing records.
- **Employee:** Completes accurate forms and training, protects credentials, and raises missing or inaccessible items promptly.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.section_title: Preboarding - accepted offer through day before start

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
| Training or acknowledgement | Normal deadline |
|---|---:|
| Account security, phishing, MFA, and incident reporting | Within 3 business days |
| Workplace conduct, harassment prevention, and reporting | Within 10 business days |
| Privacy and data-classification training | Within 10 business days |
| Role-specific safety, compliance, or customer training | Before performing the controlled activity and no later than 30 days |
| Manager responsibilities, if applicable | Within 30 calendar days |
Access to sensitive systems may be withheld or suspended until required training is complete.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
The manager should explain team goals, decision rights, communication norms, core collaboration hours, stakeholders, current priorities, and how performance will be assessed. The employee should meet key team members and know how to request help.
For Remote or Hybrid employees, the manager should verify workspace readiness, meeting access, time-zone expectations, and planned onsite requirements. Recurring work-location rules are governed by **POL-RWK-001**.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
### 30-day checkpoint
Confirm role clarity, essential access, required training, payroll accuracy, benefit enrollment status, equipment, and immediate support needs.
### 60-day checkpoint
Review performance feedback, collaboration, workload, learning plan, and suitability of any recurring remote arrangement that was not established in the offer.
### 90-day checkpoint
Assess progress against initial outcomes, complete outstanding onboarding items, confirm ongoing development priorities, and close or extend the onboarding case. A checkpoint is not a guarantee of employment or a substitute for ordinary performance management.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: People Operations issues eligibility and enrollment notices under **POL-BEN-001**. Employees must complete elections within the stated window. Payroll questions should be reported promptly and not deferred until the 30-day checkpoint.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
IT provides the standard kit for the employee's designation under **POL-EQP-001**. Employees should not purchase a laptop or other technology expecting reimbursement. Eligible ergonomic furniture requires preapproval and is subject to the policy cap.
Equipment shipped before the start date must remain unopened by anyone other than the employee and must be stored securely. Loss or damage must be reported immediately.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.section_title: Access control and segregation of duties
chunk.text:
Access must be requested by an authorized manager, approved by the system owner where required, and limited to the role. Privileged, financial, HR, production, and Restricted-data access requires enhanced review. Access should be tested, but not broadened merely for convenience.
Changes identified during onboarding must use the same approval process. Shared accounts are prohibited unless Security has approved a technical exception.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.section_title: Incomplete, delayed, or failed onboarding items
chunk.text:
A missing item should be assigned to an owner and tracked in the onboarding case. The employee should not be penalized for a company-caused delay. However, Northstar may postpone controlled work, restrict access, or adjust duties when identity, authorization, training, equipment, or security requirements are incomplete.
A material issue, such as inability to verify work authorization, suspected record falsification, safety risk, or harassment concern, must be escalated under **POL-HRC-001**.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text: Onboarding records are retained in approved HR, payroll, learning, asset, and access systems. Copies should not be stored in manager personal drives. Medical or accommodation information is stored separately with restricted access.

chunk.applicability: New employees and authorized workers completing Northstar onboarding in Canada or the United States.
chunk.text:
- A new Remote employee receives a company laptop and approved accessories; the employee does not buy a personal laptop for reimbursement.
- A finance employee may start general orientation while privileged payment access remains pending required approval.
- An employee hired as RFT on September 10 receives the benefits eligibility timeline described in **POL-BEN-001** and must enroll within the notice window.
- A missing security-training completion may lead to temporary access restriction but should be tracked and resolved, not ignored.

chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text: This policy defines standard equipment, ownership, procurement, home-office support, connectivity stipends, acceptable use, repair, replacement, loss, and return. Its goals are to provide reliable tools, control cost, protect information, and maintain accurate asset records.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
Equipment purchased or supplied by Northstar remains company property unless a written transfer says otherwise. Employees may not sell, pledge, donate, dispose of, or permanently modify company equipment.
IT procures standard technology. Employees must not purchase laptops, monitors, phones, software, cloud services, or security devices with an expectation of reimbursement unless IT and the required budget approver have approved the purchase in advance.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
Actual configuration depends on role and availability.
| Work designation | Standard technology kit |
|---|---|
| Office-Based | Company laptop, charger, dock or office connection, access to office monitor and standard keyboard/mouse, role-required headset |
| Hybrid | Company laptop, charger, dock, one home monitor, standard keyboard/mouse, and headset when required |
| Remote | Company laptop, charger, dock, up to two monitors based on role, standard keyboard/mouse, headset, and webcam when needed |
A role may require specialized hardware, mobile device, security key, testing equipment, or accessibility technology. Non-standard equipment requires the relevant system owner, IT, and budget approval.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
RFT and RPT employees with a current Hybrid or Remote designation may request preapproval for ergonomic furniture reimbursement up to **CAD 500 or USD 375 once every 36 months**. The combined limit may cover an approved chair, desk, footrest, keyboard tray, or similar ergonomic item.
The employee must submit the request before purchase and follow **POL-EXP-001**. Amounts above the limit are personal unless People Operations approves a workplace accommodation. Office-Based employees are not normally eligible because the assigned office is the primary workspace.
Reimbursed furniture normally becomes the employee's property and is not returned, unless the approval states that Northstar is purchasing and owning the item.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
A Remote-designated employee may receive a monthly internet stipend of **CAD 50 or USD 40** through payroll or the approved stipend process. Hybrid and Office-Based employees are not normally eligible unless a written agreement or accommodation says otherwise.
The stipend supports ordinary service and does not require the employee to provide personal browsing history or a detailed household bill. It does not guarantee reimbursement of the full internet cost. Business travel connectivity is handled under **POL-EXP-001**.
Company-paid mobile service is role-based. Employees should not use a personal phone as the primary repository for company information. When personal mobile enrollment is approved, company data may be remotely removed without affecting personal content to the extent technically possible.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
IT records the asset identifier, assigned user, serial number, configuration, issue date, and status. Employees must verify receipt and promptly report an error. Company devices should not be transferred between employees without IT authorization.
Equipment must be kept in a reasonably secure, clean, and ventilated location. Food, liquids, pets, children, visitors, and environmental conditions should be managed to reduce damage or unauthorized use.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
Limited incidental personal use is allowed when lawful, reasonable, secure, and not disruptive. Employees must not use equipment for unlawful activity, harassment, outside commercial work, cryptocurrency mining, unapproved high-risk software, or content that violates **POL-CON-001**.
Only approved software, extensions, and peripherals may be installed. Security controls, encryption, management agents, logs, and update settings must not be disabled.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
Employees should report faults through IT support and must not use an unapproved repair shop. IT decides whether to troubleshoot, repair, loan, or replace equipment.
Planning assumptions are a four-year laptop lifecycle and five-year monitor lifecycle, but replacement depends on security support, performance, condition, and business need. Lifecycle timing is not a personal entitlement to a new model.
Damage from normal use is covered by Northstar. Negligent, repeated, or intentional damage may be reviewed with People Operations, but managers must not deduct costs from pay without lawful authorization.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
Loss or theft of a company device, security key, badge, or phone used for MFA must be reported to IT/Security and the manager within one hour of discovery, following **POL-SEC-001**. The employee should provide location, time, device, and known circumstances and cooperate with remote lock, credential reset, police report, or insurer process.
Safety takes priority over recovering property. Employees must not confront a suspected thief.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text: Equipment taken outside the registered province, state, or country is subject to **POL-INT-001** and **POL-SEC-001**. Security may issue a temporary travel device, restrict data, or prohibit specific equipment. Employees must not place company equipment in checked baggage unless no safer option exists and Security has approved it.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text:
Employees must return requested equipment in the condition reasonably expected from normal use:
- within seven calendar days after employment ends, unless the separation notice provides a shorter lawful period;
- before or promptly after a role or location change when IT requests different equipment; and
- immediately when access is suspended for a material security reason.
IT provides return instructions and, when appropriate, prepaid shipping. Employees must not wipe, reset, or discard a device before return.

chunk.applicability: Employees and authorized workers issued company equipment or approved for home-office equipment.
chunk.policy_title: Company Equipment and Home Office Equipment
chunk.text: An employee who needs non-standard equipment for a disability, injury, or ergonomic restriction should contact People Operations. Accommodation-related equipment is assessed separately from the ordinary furniture cap and may require functional information, but not unnecessary diagnosis disclosure to the manager.

chunk.text: Employees safeguard and return equipment. Managers identify role needs and approve legitimate non-standard requests. IT procures, supports, inventories, and disposes of assets. Security defines controls and incident response. Finance audits expenditures. People Operations handles accommodation and conduct questions.

chunk.text:
Northstar is committed to a respectful, safe, inclusive, honest, and professional environment. Everyone covered by
this policy must treat others with dignity, protect company and personal information, avoid improper conflicts, and
report material concerns in good faith.
This policy applies in offices, remote work, business travel, customer sites, online communication, work events,
social functions connected to work, and interactions involving company systems or authority.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Expected conduct includes professional communication, reasonable collaboration, respect for boundaries, con-
structive disagreement, inclusive participation, and compliance with lawful instructions. A demanding deadline,
