informal channel, remote setting, or senior title does not excuse abusive behavior.
Examples of unacceptable conduct include bullying, humiliation, threats, repeated hostile comments, deliberate
exclusion used as punishment, sabotage, and misuse of authority. Ordinary feedback, performance management,
or respectful disagreement is not misconduct merely because it is uncomfortable.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Harassment, discrimination, and sexual harassment are prohibited on any protected or personal characteristic
recognized by applicable law or company policy. Prohibited behavior may be verbal, visual, physical, digital, or
sexual and may occur even without intent to offend.
Examples include slurs, degrading jokes, unwanted sexual attention, repeated comments about a person’s body or
identity, display of offensive material, conditioning work opportunities on personal or sexual conduct, and adverse
treatment because a person raised a concern or requested accommodation.
A single severe incident or a pattern of less severe incidents may violate this policy.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Retaliation is prohibited against a person who in good faith reports a concern, asks a question, participates in an
investigation, requests leave or accommodation, refuses an unlawful instruction, or supports another person.
Retaliation may include termination, demotion, threats, schedule manipulation, exclusion, hostile scrutiny, reduced
opportunity, negative references, or social pressure. A good-faith report is protected even when the concern is not
substantiated. Knowingly false statements may be addressed separately.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Violence, credible threats, stalking, intimidation, weapons contrary to law or site rules, and intentional property
damage are prohibited. In an immediate danger, contact local emergency services first, move to safety, and then
notify Security or People Operations when possible.
Do not use an ordinary HR case or AI assistant as the only response to an emergency.

chunk.section_title: Conflicts of interest and outside activity
chunk.text:
Employees must disclose an actual or potential conflict, including a financial interest in a supplier or customer,
outside work that competes or interferes, supervision of a close personal relationship, or participation in a decision
affecting a related person.
Disclosure does not automatically prohibit the activity. Northstar may approve safeguards, change decision author-
ity, or determine that the conflict cannot be managed. Employees must not use confidential information, company
time, equipment, or position for improper personal benefit.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Gifts or entertainment must be modest, infrequent, lawful, transparent, and consistent with POL-EXP-001. Cash
or cash equivalents are prohibited. Anything intended to influence a decision, reward improper conduct, or create
an obligation must not be offered or accepted.
Government, healthcare, education, and regulated-sector interactions may require Legal or Compliance review
even below ordinary limits.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Employees must protect Confidential and Restricted information and comply with POL-SEC-001. Access is based
on role need, not curiosity. Personnel, customer, investigation, payroll, and security information must not be dis-
cussed with unauthorized people or placed in public AI tools.

Employees must preserve relevant records when notified of an investigation, audit, legal hold, or security incident.
Altering, hiding, or destroying evidence is prohibited.

chunk.section_title: Communication, social media, and public statements
chunk.text:
Employees may express personal views, but must not imply company endorsement without authority, disclose non-
public information, harass colleagues, or use company branding deceptively. Only authorized spokespersons may
make official public statements.
Work communication should remain professional. Recording a meeting requires notice and must comply with law
and policy. Managers must not require employees to disclose personal social-media passwords.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.section_title: Substance use and fitness for work
chunk.text:
Employees must be fit to perform duties safely and effectively. Possessing, distributing, or working while impaired
by unlawful drugs or misused substances is prohibited. Lawful medication or disability-related needs should be
discussed confidentially with People Operations when they may affect safety or require accommodation.
Alcohol may be served at an approved event, but participation is optional and standards of conduct remain in force.

Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
A manager who receives or observes a concern involving harassment, discrimination, retaliation, violence, cred-
ible threat, serious safety risk, fraud, or material confidentiality breach must notify People Operations, Ethics, or
Security within one business day - sooner when risk is urgent. The manager must not promise secrecy, conduct
an unauthorized investigation, or require the reporter to confront the subject.
Routine interpersonal issues may be coached locally, but a manager should consult People Operations when clas-
sification is uncertain.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
Northstar will assess concerns promptly and impartially. An investigation may include interviews, documents, sys-
tem records, and other relevant evidence. Participants must cooperate honestly and preserve confidentiality to the
extent possible.
The subject of a concern will receive a fair opportunity to respond, consistent with safety, privacy, and investiga-
tive integrity. Northstar may use interim measures such as reporting-line changes, access restrictions, schedule
changes, or paid leave. Interim measures are not findings of misconduct.
Northstar T echnologies Inc. Internal Policy - Synthetic Corpus

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
When a concern is substantiated, action may include coaching, training, process changes, warning, reassignment,
loss of access, contract action, termination, restitution, or external referral. Outcomes are based on severity, intent,
impact, history, consistency, and legal obligations.
Reporters and witnesses may be told that the matter was addressed, but privacy may prevent disclosure of detailed
discipline.

chunk.applicability: Employees, managers, contractors, applicants, and workplace participants interacting with Northstar.
chunk.text:
• A manager who receives a harassment complaint must escalate it within one business day and should not
attempt a private settlement.
• An employee may disclose a supplier family relationship and be removed from the selection decision without
being accused of wrongdoing.
• Repeatedly excluding an employee from essential meetings after the employee reported misconduct may be
retaliation.
• An immediate threat of violence requires emergency and Security action, not only a standard HR ticket.

This policy provides a controlled process for receiving, classifying, prioritizing, assigning, documenting, escalating,
and closing HR cases. It supports timely service while protecting confidentiality, safety, evidence, and fair process.

chunk.text:
The HR case system and AI assistant are not emergency services. A person facing immediate danger, active
violence, urgent medical need, or an ongoing crime should contact local emergency services and move to safety.
Security should be notified as soon as possible for an immediate workplace or information-security threat.

explicit user confirmation. It must not make a final misconduct finding, diagnose a condition, promise confidentiality,
send a message, alter an employee record, or take an irreversible action.

chunk.text:
Case information is Confidential or Restricted depending on content. Access is limited by role and need. Managers
generally receive only the information needed to act; they are not automatically entitled to medical details, witness
statements, or disciplinary records.
Northstar cannot promise absolute confidentiality. Information may be shared to investigate, protect people, admin-
ister leave or benefits, obtain advice, comply with law, or provide fair process. Anonymous reporting is accepted,
but limited information may constrain the response.

The case owner defines scope, issues, witnesses, documents, system data, and decision authority. Evidence
should be collected lawfully, preserved, and recorded with source and date. Investigators must distinguish allega-
tion, evidence, finding, and recommendation.
The AI assistant may summarize supplied synthetic information but must not infer guilt, credibility, protected status,
medical diagnosis, or legal conclusion. Human review is required for sensitive triage and all findings.

The reporter should receive an acknowledgement, safe contact method, and reasonable updates. Northstar may
implement interim measures such as access restriction, reporting-line separation, schedule change, remote work,
no-contact direction, paid leave, payroll correction, or security controls.
Interim measures protect people or evidence and are not disciplinary findings. Retaliation concerns must be treated
as a new or linked case and assessed promptly.

nications, and any follow-up date. A case may close as answered, corrected, referred, resolved, unsubstantiated,

modation, and significant ethics cases are normally retained for seven years after closure, or longer when law, plan
terms, litigation hold, or the corporate schedule requires. Access logs and deletion must follow approved records
and security processes.

People Operations periodically reviews response times, priority accuracy, repeat issues, handoffs, privacy incidents,
and user feedback. Metrics must not encourage premature closure or discourage sensitive reporting.
Retaliation for good-faith reporting, participation, or use of a protected process is prohibited and should be reported
as a P2 or P1 case depending on risk.
